milestones.name: ATC Flight Plan Activated
rules: To check consistency between ATC Flight Plan, Airport Slot and Airport flight data before the first E-DPI is sent.

The AO must provide correct information before the first E-DPI message, in order to feed Network Operations with consistent SOBT, aircraft registration, and first destination data, as early in time as possible.
The E-DPI message should not be sent if no or inconsistent information is provided.
This process is triggered by the first activation of the ATC Flight Plan (earliest EOBT-3 hr), or new or late submissions of the ATC Flight Plan, after cancellation or revised EOBT.
ELDT and EIBT updated for an arrival, EOBT and ETOT updated for a departure.
The flight is ready not later than 15 minutes after the planned EOBT.
The DPI process commences the correct messaging with Network Operations (if implemented).

milestones.name: EOBT - 2 hr
rules: The CTOT is issued by Network Operations at EOBT-2h if the flight is regulated.
For inbound flights, ELDT is updated based on information provided by the FUM messages, taking into account the actual progress of the flight.
To check whether AO/GH flight estimates are consistent with the ATC Flight Plan, before or after take off from outstation.
To inform Network Operations about the updated take off time estimate using a T-DPI Message at EOBT-2 hrs.
Calculation basis for the TTOT shall take into account EIBT+MTTT+EXOT, if later than EOBT+EXOT.
In the case of manual input of TOBT, this estimate overrides the EIBT+MTTT estimate, hence TTOT equals TOBT+EXOT.
This procedure is triggered by a time stamp, at EOBT-2h.
Mark appropriate fields as REGULATED.

milestones.name: Take Off from Outstation
rules: The outstation provides ATOT to the Network Operations and Aircraft Operator.
The accuracy of ATOT is +/- 1 minute.

If the departure airport is more than 3hrs flying time from the destination airport the ATOT is received from either the Network Operations FUM or via the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler, and ELDT is calculated using the ATOT and the Estimated Elapsed Time on the FPL.

If the flight is within 3hrs flying time of the destination airport the Network Operations monitors progress of the flight using the ETFMS and sends a Flight Update Message (FUM) that provides updates of the flight's progress.

To check whether the AO/GH estimated landing times after take off from outstation are consistent with the outbound ATC Flight Plan, and when needed inform the Network Operations about the updated take off time estimates using a T-DPI-t Message.
A TTOT tolerance of 5 minutes is respected before Network Operations is informed of the updated TTOT.
Calculation basis for the TTOT shall take into account EIBT+MTTT+EXOT.
In case EOBT is later than EIBT+MTTT, TTOT equals EOBT+EXOT.
In the case where TOBT is available this prediction overrules the EIBT+MTTT estimate, hence TTOT equals TOBT+EXOT.
This process is triggered by the take off from outstation.

milestones.name: Local Radar Update
rules: The radar system is able to detect a flight based upon the assigned SSR code when the flight crosses a defined FIR/ATC boundary.
Update of the ELDT can trigger a new TOBT to be entered by the AO/GH, or calculated automatically by the Airport CDM Platform.
Taking into account the taxi-in time (EXIT), any change to a stand or gate is not preferred after ELDT-30'.
An estimated in-block time (EIBT) is computed using the ELDT and the estimated taxi-in time.
To commence the TOBT process and check whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT.
This process is triggered by the detection of the flight by radar in either FIR, TMA, or on Final Approach.

milestones.name: Final Approach
rules: The radar system detects a flight based upon the assigned SSR code and identifies when the flight crosses either a defined range/position or passes/leaves a predetermined level.
Update of the ELDT determines a new TOBT.
To commence the TOBT process and check whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT.
This process is triggered by the detection of the flight by radar in either FIR, TMA, or on Final Approach.

milestones.name: Landed
rules: ALDT is provided by ATC system or by ACARS from equipped aircraft.
Data is available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.

The occurrence of ALDT triggers an update of downstream estimates: TOBT and TTOT are updated automatically or inserted manually by the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler, calculated on the basis of the defined turn-round period for the departing flight.
The EIBT can be updated according to the ALDT + EXIT.
To check whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT or ATC Flight Plan.
This process is triggered by Actual Landing Time: ALDT.

milestones.name: In-Block
rules: AIBT is provided by ACARS equipped aircraft or automated docking systems or ATC systems or by manual input.
Data is available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.

The occurrence of AIBT should trigger an update of downstream estimates: TOBT and TTOT are updated automatically or inserted manually by the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler, calculated on the basis of the estimated turn-round period for the departing flight.
To check whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT or ATC Flight Plan.
This process is triggered by Actual In Blocks Time: AIBT.
other_concepts: ACGT considered to commence at AIBT

milestones.name: Ground Handling Started
rules: The occurrence of ACGT triggers an update of downstream estimates: TOBT is updated automatically or inserted manually by the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler, calculated on the basis of the estimated turn-round period for the departing flight.
To check whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT or ATC Flight Plan.
This process is triggered by Actual Commence of Ground Handling: ACGT.
other_concepts: ACGT specific to first operation of the day or long term parked flights

milestones.name: Final Confirmation of the TOBT
rules: The Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler provides the information t minutes before EOBT (t is a parameter time agreed locally).

Following the receipt of the TOBT, the ATC system will calculate and provide the Estimated Taxi-Out Time (EXOT) based on the predicted traffic load, gate/stand location, runway in use, and waiting period at the Holding Position.
The flight is introduced into the pre-departure sequence.
To check whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check should be performed at a predefined time (local parameter) to confirm TOBT prior to TSAT issue and verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan estimates given the updated TOBT.
No need to confirm an existing TOBT if it has been manually modified before.
This process is triggered by a new TOBT or TTOT update.
other_concepts: difference between EOBT and TOBT in disruptions

milestones.name: TSAT Issued
rules: To inform all relevant partners of the TSAT that has been allocated to the flight.
The Network Operations is informed by a T-DPI-s for non regulated flights.
To check whether the number of TOBT updates exceeds a tolerance defined locally, after TSAT has been issued.
In case the number of TOBT updates exceeds a threshold, the TOBT input should be processed according to local procedure.
This process is triggered by a defined time (local parameter) before TOBT, or TOBT update after TSAT issue.

milestones.name: Boarding Starts
rules: To inform all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Start Boarding Time (ASBT) when it occurs.
To check whether boarding starts in time to respect TOBT and inform the AO/GH in case TOBT needs to be updated.
At a certain time before TOBT (local variable e.g. corresponding to aircraft type) a check shall be performed to check the boarding status.
This process is triggered by a time variable <value> minutes before TOBT.
other_concepts: air-bridge/pier, aircraft steps, coaching to a stand

milestones.name: Aircraft Ready
rules: To inform all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Ready Time (ARDT) in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft is ready for start up/push-back.
To inform the AO/GH that TOBT has passed and the Airport CDM Platform has not yet received ARDT or Ready Status (RDY).
At TOBT + tolerance the AO/GH are informed that TOBT has passed and there has not been a ready status message yet.
ATC refines the pre-departure sequence.
This procedure is triggered by an input to the Airport CDM Platform.
other_concepts: pilot requests start up just before TSAT

milestones.name: Start Up Requested
rules: To inform all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Start up Request Time (ASRT) in the Airport CDM Platform.
To alert all relevant Airport CDM Partners when no start up has been requested inside the locally agreed TSAT tolerance window.
If the start up request is not made by TSAT + tolerance, the AO/GH is informed that no start up has been requested, and should update TOBT.
ATC confirms TSAT to the pilot in order to maintain the aircraft in the pre-departure sequence.
Timestamp when the tolerance window has passed at TSAT.
other_concepts: ATC assures regulated flight respects CTOT

milestones.name: Start Up Approved
rules: To inform all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual start up approval Time (ASAT) in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft has received start up approval/push-back clearance.
To check if ASAT is in accordance to TSAT and to alert all relevant Airport CDM Partners when no start up has been granted.
In case the start up approval is not granted at TSAT + tolerance, all relevant partners should be informed.
The flight will be re-sequenced.
This process is triggered by start up request by flight crew (voice or DCL) or a locally defined time around TSAT if Milestone Process 13 is omitted.
other_concepts: aircraft will start up, push back and start to taxi on receipt of ATC approval

milestones.name: Off-Block
rules: To inform all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Off-Block Time (AOBT) in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft has commenced push-back/taxi from parking position.
TTOT updated considering the EXOT.
AOBT always triggers an A-DPI message to Network Operations or, in the case of remote holding, at a defined time prior to TTOT.
After a first A-DPI is sent this check shall be performed to check TTOT updates against the TTOT tolerance before Network Operations is informed, with a new A-DPI, of the updated TTOT.
This process is triggered by AOBT detection.

milestones.name: Take Off
rules: ATOT is provided by ATC system or from ACARS equipped aircraft.
Data is available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.
FSA and MVT messages are sent.
To inform all relevant Airport CDM Partners about the actual take off.
An airborne message is generated and the flight is removed from the departure sequence.
This process is triggered by Tower FDPS, A-SMGCS/Radar detection or ACARS.
